html:
A Dutch navigator in the service of the Dutch East India Company who in 1642 became the first recorded European to reach Tasmania and New Zealand.

Born in Groningen province, he went to Asia in 1633. In 1642 Governor General Anthony van Diemen sent him from Batavia to find the great southern land and a sea route to Chile. Sailing south of Australia, which he never saw, he sighted a coast in November 1642 and named it Van Diemen's Land, now Tasmania. In December he reached New Zealand, which he called Staten Landt. At Golden Bay, Māori canoes rammed one of his boats and four of his men were killed, and he never landed.

He sailed on to Tonga and Fiji and back to Batavia by New Guinea. In 1644 he charted much of Australia's north coast. The Company was disappointed: he had found no gold and no trade. But his charts showed that Australia was not joined to a polar continent. James Cook used them more than a century later. See also the first European landing in Australia.
sum: A Dutch navigator in the service of the Dutch East India Company who in 1642 became the first recorded European to reach Tasmania and New Zealand.
